So he said: ﴿O my people, what is (the matter) with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?﴾ That is: tell me about your situation. I call you to salvation from the Fire and to entering Paradise through faith in God and obedience to His messengers, while you call me to the Fire by what you want from me of shirk (associating others with God).

It has been said: the meaning of ﴿ma li﴾ (what is with me) is "what is (the matter) with you that I call you," as you say, "What is with me that I see you sad?", meaning "What is with you?"

Then he explained the two calls, saying: ﴿You call me to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge﴾. So the phrase ﴿tad'unani﴾ (you call me) is either a substitute (badal) for the first ﴿tad'unani﴾ or an explanation of it. ﴿Of which I have no knowledge﴾ means: I have no knowledge that it is a partner of God. ﴿And I call you to the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving﴾: that is, to the Almighty in His retribution against those who disbelieve, and the Oft-Forgiving toward the sin of those who believe in Him.

﴿Lā jaram﴾ (certainly/undoubtedly): the explanation of this has already been given in Surah Hud. ﴿Jaram﴾ is a past-tense verb with the meaning of ﴿ḥaqqa﴾ (it is true/due). The ﴿lā﴾ that precedes it is for negating what they claimed and refuting what they asserted. The subject of this verb is His saying: ﴿that what you call me to has no call (no efficacy) in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, that is: it is established and necessary that the call to it is void.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that it has no answered call that benefits. It has also been said: it has no call that would entitle it to divinity in this world or in the Hereafter.

Al-Kalbi said: it has no intercession. ﴿And that our return is to God﴾: that is, our place of return and our destination is to Him, first through death and then through resurrection, and He will repay each person with what he deserves of good and evil. ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾: that is, those who greatly increase their disobedience to God. Qatadah and Ibn Sirin said: it means the polytheists. Mujahid and al-Sha'bi said: they are the foolish, those who shed blood unjustly. Ikrimah said: the tyrants and the arrogant. It has also been said: they are those who transgress the limits of God. The ﴿anna﴾ (that) in both places is coordinated (ʿatf) with the ﴿anna﴾ in His saying ﴿that what you call me to﴾, and the meaning is: and it is true that our return is to God, and it is true that the transgressors, etc.

﴿So you will remember what I say to you﴾: when the punishment descends upon you, and you will know that I have indeed exerted myself in advising and admonishing you. In this vagueness there is a threat and intimidation that is not hidden. ﴿And I entrust my affair to God﴾: that is, I rely upon Him and surrender my affair to Him.

It has been said: he said this when they intended to harm him. Muqatil said: this believing man fled to the mountain and they could not reach him. It has also been said: the speaker is Moses, but the first (view) is preferable.

﴿So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾ (p-1303): that is, God protected him from the evil plot and the harm they intended for him. Qatadah said: God delivered him along with the Children of Israel.

﴿And there befell the people of Pharaoh the terrible punishment﴾: that is, it encompassed them and descended upon them, the evil punishment.

Al-Kisa'i said: one says ﴿ḥaqa yaḥīqu ḥayqan wa-ḥuyūqan﴾ (it befell, it encompassed) when it descends and clings. Al-Kalbi said: they drowned in the sea and entered the Fire. By ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾ is meant Pharaoh and his people; he omitted mention of him explicitly because mention of his people suffices, as he is more entitled to it than they are. Or it is meant that ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾ refers to Pharaoh himself.

The first is preferable, because they were all punished in this world by drowning, and they will be punished in the Hereafter by the Fire.

Then He, glorified is He, explained what had been stated in general about the evil punishment, saying: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾. The ﴿al-nār﴾ (the Fire) is nominative as a substitute (badal) for ﴿sū' al-ʿadhāb﴾ (the evil punishment). It has also been said: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, or it is a subject whose predicate is ﴿yu'raḍūna﴾ (they are exposed). The first is preferable, and al-Zajjaj preferred it. On the last two readings, the sentence is a new sentence (mustaʾnafa) answering an implied question.

It was also read in the accusative (al-nār), on the assumption of a verb implied by ﴿yu'raḍūna﴾ in meaning, i.e., "they lead the Fire, they are exposed to it," or on the basis of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Farra' permitted the genitive (al-nāri) as a substitution for ﴿al-ʿadhāb﴾.

The majority held that this exposure is in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and it has been said: it is in the Hereafter.

Al-Farra' said: there is in the verse an inversion (taqdīm and taʾkhīr), i.e., "Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment, the Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening." But there is no need for this strained reading, for His saying ﴿And on the day the Hour arises: admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾ clearly indicates that this exposure is in the barzakh. His saying ﴿admit﴾ is by implied speech: it is said to the angels, "Admit the people of Pharaoh," and ﴿the most severe punishment﴾ is the punishment of the Fire.

Ḥamzah, al-Kisa'i, Nafi' and Ḥafṣ read ﴿adkhilū﴾ with an open hamzah and a kasrah on the kha', and this is on the assumption of implied speech as mentioned. The rest read ﴿udkhulū﴾ with a hamzat al-waṣl (connecting hamzah) from ﴿dakhala yadkhulu﴾ as an imperative to the people of Pharaoh to enter, with the vocative particle implied: i.e., "Enter, O people of Pharaoh, the most severe punishment."

﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire﴾: the adverbial clause (al-ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed by an implied ﴿udhkur﴾ (remember).

The meaning: Remember for your people the time when they dispute with one another in the Fire. Then He, glorified is He, explained this dispute, saying: ﴿So the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾, regarding submission to the prophets and following them, and they are the leaders of disbelief. ﴿Indeed, we were following you﴾: ﴿tabaʿan﴾ (followers) is the plural of ﴿tābiʿ﴾, like ﴿khadam﴾ and ﴿khādim﴾ (servants), or it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) functioning in the position of the active participle, i.e., "following," or there is an omitted genitive, i.e., "possessors of following." The Basrans said: ﴿tabaʿ﴾ can be singular and can be plural. The Kufans said it is a plural with no singular. ﴿So will you bear for us a portion of the Fire?﴾: that is, will you ward off from us a portion of it or carry it with us? The accusative of ﴿naṣīban﴾ (a portion) is by an implied verb indicated by ﴿mughnūna﴾ (you bear/avert), i.e., "will you ward off from us a portion, or prevent (it)," on the basis of implying the meaning of ﴿ḥāmilīn﴾ (carrying), i.e., "will you be carrying with us a portion?", or on the basis of it being a verbal noun.

﴿Those who were arrogant said: we are all in it﴾: this sentence is a new sentence answering an implied question, and the meaning is: we and you together are in Hell, so how can we avail you?

The majority read ﴿kullun﴾ (all) in the nominative, as the subject, with ﴿fīhā﴾ (in it) as its predicate, and the clause is the predicate of ﴿inna﴾ (indeed), as al-Akhfash said. Ibn al-Sumayfa' and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ﴿kullan﴾ in the accusative. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: it is for emphasis of the subject of ﴿inna﴾, with the meaning of ﴿kullunā﴾ (all of us), and its tanwin (nunation) is a substitute for the omitted genitive. It has also been said: it is in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl), and Ibn Mālik preferred this.

﴿Indeed God has judged between the servants﴾: that is, He decided between them, that a group is in Paradise and a group is in the blazing Fire.

﴿And those who are in the Fire will say﴾, from the disbelieving nations, their arrogant and their weak, ﴿to the keepers of Hell﴾: ﴿khazana﴾ is the plural of ﴿khāzin﴾ (keeper), who is the one in charge of punishing the people of the Fire. ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us one day of the punishment﴾: ﴿yawman﴾ (a day) is an adverbial of time governed by ﴿yukhaffif﴾ (lighten), and the object of ﴿yukhaffif﴾ is omitted: i.e., lighten for us some of the punishment to the extent of a day, or within a day.

The clause ﴿Did not your messengers used to come to you with clear proofs?﴾ is a new sentence answering an implied question, and the interrogative is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿They said: Yes﴾: that is, they came to us with them, but we denied them and did not believe in them, nor in what they brought of clear arguments. When they acknowledged this, the angels, who are the keepers of Hell, said to them, ﴿So call (upon Him)﴾: that is, if the matter is as such, then you call, for we do not call upon (Him) for one who disbelieved in God and denied His messengers after their coming with clear proofs.

Then they informed them that their call would not benefit anything, so they said: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾: that is, in loss, void, ruin, and destruction.

The clause ﴿Indeed We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe﴾ is a new sentence from His side, glorified is He: that is, We will make them the victors over their enemies and the subduers of them. The relative pronoun (al-mawṣūl) is in the accusative position, coordinated (ʿaṭf) with ﴿rusulanā﴾ (Our messengers), i.e., "We will surely help Our messengers, and We will help those who believe along with them in the life of this world," by what God has accustomed them of retribution against them through killing, plundering, capturing, and subjugation, ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿al-ashhād﴾ (the witnesses) are the angels and the prophets.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: ﴿al-ashhād﴾ are the angels, who bear witness for the prophets that they conveyed (the message), and against the nations that they denied.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿al-ashhād﴾ is the plural of ﴿shāhid﴾ (witness), like ﴿ṣāḥib﴾ and ﴿aṣḥāb﴾ (companion, companions). Al-Nahhas said: the pattern fāʿil is not (normally) pluralized to afʿāl, and it is not analogized upon; rather, whatever comes of it heard (from the Arabs) is recited as it is heard. So it is, on this view, the plural of ﴿shahīd﴾, like ﴿sharīf﴾ and ﴿ashrāf﴾. The meaning of their being helped on the day when the witnesses stand is that God will recompense them for their deeds, so He admits them to Paradise and honors them with His honors, and He recompenses the disbelievers for their deeds, so He curses them and admits them to the Fire.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿On the day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse﴾: that is, distance from mercy, and for them is the evil abode, that is, the Fire. ﴿The day﴾ (yawma) is a substitute for ﴿yawma yaqūmu al-ashhād﴾ (the day the witnesses stand). Their excuse did not benefit them because it was a false excuse, a rejected pretext, and a deviant doubt.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿tanfaʿu﴾ (will benefit) with the feminine (taʾ fawqiyya, upper ta'), and Nafi' and the Kufans read it with the masculine (yāʾ taḥtiyya, lower yā'). Both are permissible in the language.

Al-Bukhari recorded in his Tarikh, and Ibn al-Mundhir (recorded) from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying ﴿and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾, that he said: they are the shedders of blood unjustly.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others recorded from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him in the morning and the evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then (it is shown) from the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then (it is shown) from the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat, until God resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.'" Ibn Mardawayh added: "Then he recited, ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾."

Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab recorded from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No doer of good, whether a Muslim or a disbeliever, does good except that God rewards him." We said: "O Messenger of God, what is the reward of the disbeliever?" He said: "Wealth, children, health, and the like of that." We said: "And what is his reward in the Hereafter?" He said: "A punishment less than the (full) punishment." And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited, ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others recorded from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him in the morning and the evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then (it is shown) from the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then (it is shown) from the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat, until God resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.'" Ibn Mardawayh added: "Then he recited, ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾."

Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab recorded from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No doer of good, whether a Muslim or a disbeliever, does good except that God rewards him." We said: "O Messenger of God, what is the reward of the disbeliever?" He said: "Wealth, children, health, and the like of that." We said: "And what is his reward in the Hereafter?" He said: "A punishment less than the (full) punishment." And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited, ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾.

Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it ḥasan), Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab recorded from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother, God will ward the Fire of Hell from his face on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited, ﴿Indeed We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe﴾. Ibn Mardawayh recorded a similar (report) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 40, verses 53–70 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾. This is part of what Allah, glorified is He, related shortly after His support for His messengers. That is, We gave him the Torah and prophethood, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. Muqatil said: "The guidance from misguidance" means the Torah.

﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book, a guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾. The Book here means the Torah. The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is that when Allah, glorified is He, revealed the Torah to Moses, it remained among them after him, and they inherited it from one generation to the next.

It was also said: the Book here means all the books revealed to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. "A guidance and a reminder" are in the accusative position, as either a *maf'ul li-ajlihi* (object of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and reminder") or as two verbal nouns in the position of a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier), meaning "guiding" and "reminding." "People of understanding" means people of sound intellect.

Then Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient in the face of harm, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah which He made to His messengers is true, with no breach in it and no doubt about its occurrence, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and His saying: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173]. Al-Kalbi said: this was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*ayat al-sayf*, a term for the verse commonly held to abrogate earlier verses calling for forbearance toward the disbelievers).

Then He commanded him, glorified is He, to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was said: the sin here means the sin of your community, so it involves an elided noun (*hadhf mudaf*). It was said: it means minor sins, according to those who permit them for the prophets. It was said: it is merely an act of worship directed to him (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness, for the increase of reward. Allah had already forgiven him what was before and what came after of his sins. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾. That is: remain in glorifying Allah, accompanied by praise of Him. It was also said: it means pray at these two times, the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was also said: they are two prayers, two rak'ahs in the morning and two rak'ahs in the evening, and that was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾. That is: without any clear, manifest proof having come to them from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾. That is: there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance toward the truth, which drives them to deny you. The clause ﴿they will never attain it﴾ (*ma hum bi-balighihi*) is a qualifying clause (*sifah*) for "pride." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain in their desire for it, so he took it to involve an elided noun. Others said: "they will never attain the pride." Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride (*takabbur*) over Muhammad (ﷺ) and greed that they might overcome him, and they will never attain that. It was also said: "pride" here means a great matter, i.e. they seek prophethood, or they seek some great matter by which they might reach you, such as killing, and they will not reach that. Mujahid said: its meaning is, in their breasts is greatness, which they will never attain. The verse refers to the polytheists, and it was also said: the Jews, as its explanation will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

Then Allah commanded him to seek refuge in Allah from their evils, saying: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. That is: turn to Him for refuge from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you. Indeed, He hears their words and sees their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Then He, glorified is He, explained His immense power, saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. That is: it is greater in souls and more magnificent in hearts, because of the enormity of their bodies, their stability without pillars, and the orbits of the spheres moving with the stars without any apparent cause. So how can they deny resurrection and the bringing back to life of what is lesser than them in every respect, as in His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal, when the Jews magnified him. Yahya ibn Salam said: this is an argument against the deniers of resurrection, meaning: they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. (p-1305) ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ the greatness of Allah's power, and that nothing can overcome Him.

Then, after He, glorified is He, mentioned disputing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, saying: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾. That is: the one who disputes with falsehood and the one who disputes with truth. ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the one who does evil﴾. That is: the doer of good through faith and righteous deeds and the doer of evil through disbelief and sins are not equal. The addition of *la* (no) in ﴿nor the evildoer﴾ is for emphasis. ﴿Little do you remember.﴾ The majority read *yatadhakkarun* with a *ya* (third person, the absent), and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading, because what comes before and after it is in the third person, not the second person. The Kufans read it with a *ta* (second person), by way of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person, i.e. "you" instead of "they"), meaning: *taddhakkur* (remembrance), "little do you remember."

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾. That is: there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence. ﴿But most of mankind do not believe﴾ in it, nor do they affirm it, due to the shortcomings of their understanding and the weakness of their intellects in grasping the proof. The "most of mankind" here means the disbelievers who deny resurrection.

Then, after He, glorified is He, made clear that the establishment of the Hour is true, with no doubt or dubiety about it, He guided His servants to what is the means to happiness in the abode of eternity. So He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to relate what He commanded him to convey, which is: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you."﴾ Most of the exegetes said the meaning is: "Make Me one and worship Me, and I will accept your worship and forgive you." It was also said: the call here means asking, i.e. seeking benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the first is preferable, because *du'a'* (calling/supplication) in most usages of the Noble Book means worship. I say: rather, the second is preferable, because the meaning of *du'a'* literally and in the Law is requesting. If it is used in other than that sense, it is metaphorical. Moreover, *du'a'* in itself, considering its literal meaning, is worship; indeed, it is the essence of worship, as the authentic hadith has reported. So Allah, glorified is He, commanded His servants to call upon Him and promised them a response, and His promise is true, and "the word is not changed with Him, nor does He break the promise."

Then He, glorified is He, explicitly stated that this calling, considering its literal meaning, which is requesting, is part of His worship, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾. That is: abased and debased. This is a severe warning for those who are too arrogant to call upon Allah. It contains great gentleness toward His servants and magnificent kindness to them, in that He threatens those who abandon seeking good from Him and seeking protection from evil through Him with this severe threat, and punishes him with this great punishment.

So, O servants of Allah, direct your desires and rely in all your requests upon the One who commanded you to direct them to Him, guided you to rely upon Him, and guaranteed you a response when you call on Him by granting your request. He is the absolutely Generous, who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and is angry with the one who does not seek from His great bounty and vast dominion what he needs of the affairs of this world and the next. It was said: this promise of response is conditional upon His will, i.e. "I will respond to you if I wish," like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 41]. Allah knows best.

The majority read *sayadkhulun* with a *fath* on the *ya* and a *damm* on the *kha*, in the active voice (*mabni lil-fa'il*). Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Warsh, and Abu Ja'far read it with a *damm* on the *ya* and a *fath* on the *kha*, in the passive voice (*mabni lil-maf'ul*).

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned some of what He had bestowed upon His servants, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein﴾ from the movements of seeking livelihood, since He made it dark and cool, suited to rest, by repose and sleep; and ﴿the day giving sight﴾, that is, bright, so that you may see your needs therein and move about in seeking your livelihood. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, bestowing upon them His blessings, which cannot be counted. ﴿But most of mankind are not grateful﴾ for the blessings and do not acknowledge them, either because of their denial of them and disbelief in them, as is the state of the disbelievers, or because of their neglect of reflection and their failure to give the thanks that the Benefactor deserves. These are the ignorant.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him﴾. Glorified is He, in this He demonstrated the perfection of His power, which necessitates the obligation of affirming His Oneness. The majority read *khaliq* (Creator) in the nominative (*raf'*), as a predicate following the first predicate of the subject. Zayd ibn 'Ali read it in the accusative (*nasb*), as a term of specification (*ikhtisas*). ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ That is: how do you turn away from worshipping Him and divert from affirming His Oneness?

﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. That is: like this delusion, those who deny the signs of Allah and reject His Oneness are deluded.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned to them another kind of His blessings which He bestowed upon them, along with what that contains of indication of the perfection of His power and His sole right to divinity, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth as a place of settlement and the sky as a ceiling﴾. That is: a place of settlement in which you live and in which you die, and the sky as a building, meaning a firm, standing roof.

Then He explained some of His blessings concerning the souls of the servants, saying: ﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms﴾. That is: He created you in the best form. Al-Zajjaj said: He created you the best of all living creatures. The majority read *sawwarakum* with a *damm* on the *sad*, and al-A'mash and Abu Razin read it with a *kasra*. Al-Jawhari said: *Siwar* with a *kasra* on the *sad* is a dialect variant of *Suwar* with a *damm*. ﴿And He provided you with good things﴾, that is, the delicious things. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is: the abundance of His goodness and blessing.

65. ﴿He is the Living; there is no deity except Him﴾. That is: the Everlasting who does not perish, the One singled out for divinity. ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾. That is: in obedience and worship. ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is a statement (*khabar*) and within it is an implied command, meaning: "Praise Him."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it. Al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'The Dajjal will come from among us at the end of time, and he will have authority. So magnify his affair. We will do such-and-such and such-and-such.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain.﴾ He said: 'Whoever says ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ will not attain it.' So He commanded His Prophet to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal. ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ka'b al-Ahbar concerning the verse that he said: "They are the Jews. It was revealed concerning them, regarding what they were awaiting of the affair of the Dajjal."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, that he said: "The greatness of Quraysh."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, (p-1306) Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilyah*, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* transmitted from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," then he recited: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me..."﴾, and said: "Those too proud to worship Me, i.e., to call upon Me, will enter Hell in humiliation."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib transmitted from al-Bara' that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, supplication is worship. ﴿And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-'Azamah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, that he said: "Affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you."

al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, regarding the verse, that he said: "Worship Me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is seeking forgiveness."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Hakim, and Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, He will be angry with him."

Ahmad, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, and al-Tabarani narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Caution does not benefit against decree, but supplication benefits against what has descended and what has not yet descended, so you must engage in supplication."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, in Nawadir al-Usul, narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The best worship is supplication," and he recited ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari, in al-Adab, narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which worship is best? He said: A person's supplication for himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him follow its saying immediately with "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is His words: ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

It was also said: the Book here means all the books revealed to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Then He, glorified is He, explained His immense power, saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Then He commanded him, glorified is He, to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. That is: without any clear, manifest proof having come to them from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾. That is: there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance toward the truth, which drives them to deny you. The clause ﴿they will never attain it﴾ (*ma hum bi-balighihi*) is a qualifying clause (*sifah*) for "pride." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain in their desire for it, so he took it to involve an elided noun. Mujahid said: its meaning is, in their breasts is greatness, which they will never attain. The verse refers to the polytheists, and it was also said: the Jews, as its explanation will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

That is: turn to Him for refuge from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you. Indeed, He hears their words and sees their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

That is: it is greater in souls and more magnificent in hearts, because of the enormity of their bodies, their stability without pillars, and the orbits of the spheres moving with the stars without any apparent cause. Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal, when the Jews magnified him. Yahya ibn Salam said: this is an argument against the deniers of resurrection, meaning: they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. Then, after He, glorified is He, mentioned disputing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, saying: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾. That is: the one who disputes with falsehood and the one who disputes with truth. ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the one who does evil﴾. That is: the doer of good through faith and righteous deeds and the doer of evil through disbelief and sins are not equal. It was said: this promise of response is conditional upon His will, i.e. "I will respond to you if I wish," like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 41]. These are the ignorant.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him﴾. Glorified is He, in this He demonstrated the perfection of His power, which necessitates the obligation of affirming His Oneness. The majority read *khaliq* (Creator) in the nominative (*raf'*), as a predicate following the first predicate of the subject. Zayd ibn 'Ali read it in the accusative (*nasb*), as a term of specification (*ikhtisas*). ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ That is: how do you turn away from worshipping Him and divert from affirming His Oneness?

﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. That is: like this delusion, those who deny the signs of Allah and reject His Oneness are deluded.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned to them another kind of His blessings which He bestowed upon them, along with what that contains of indication of the perfection of His power and His sole right to divinity, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth as a place of settlement and the sky as a ceiling﴾. That is: a place of settlement in which you live and in which you die, and the sky as a building, meaning a firm, standing roof.

Then He explained some of His blessings concerning the souls of the servants, saying: ﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms﴾. That is: He created you in the best form. Al-Zajjaj said: He created you the best of all living creatures. The majority read *sawwarakum* with a *damm* on the *sad*, and al-A'mash and Abu Razin read it with a *kasra*. Al-Jawhari said: *Siwar* with a *kasra* on the *sad* is a dialect variant of *Suwar* with a *damm*. ﴿And He provided you with good things﴾, that is, the delicious things. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is: the abundance of His goodness and blessing.

65. ﴿He is the Living; there is no deity except Him﴾. That is: the Everlasting who does not perish, the One singled out for divinity. ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾. That is: in obedience and worship. ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is a statement (*khabar*) and within it is an implied command, meaning: "Praise Him."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it. Al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'The Dajjal will come from among us at the end of time, and he will have authority. So magnify his affair. We will do such-and-such and such-and-such.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain.﴾ He said: 'Whoever says ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ will not attain it.' So He commanded His Prophet to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal. ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ka'b al-Ahbar concerning the verse that he said: "They are the Jews. It was revealed concerning them, regarding what they were awaiting of the affair of the Dajjal."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, that he said: "The greatness of Quraysh."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, (p-1306) Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilyah*, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* transmitted from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," then he recited: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me..."﴾, and said: "Those too proud to worship Me, i.e., to call upon Me, will enter Hell in humiliation."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib transmitted from al-Bara' that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, supplication is worship. ﴿And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-'Azamah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, that he said: "Affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you."

al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, regarding the verse, that he said: "Worship Me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is seeking forgiveness."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Hakim, and Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, He will be angry with him."

Ahmad, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, and al-Tabarani narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Caution does not benefit against decree, but supplication benefits against what has descended and what has not yet descended, so you must engage in supplication."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The best worship is supplication," and he recited ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari, in al-Adab, narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which worship is best? He said: A person's supplication for himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him follow its saying immediately with "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾. This is part of what Allah, glorified is He, related shortly after His support for His messengers. Muqatil said: "The guidance from misguidance" means the Torah.

The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is that when Allah, glorified is He, revealed the Torah to Moses, it remained among them after him, and they inherited it from one generation to the next.

It was also said: the Book here means all the books revealed to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. "A guidance and a reminder" are in the accusative position, as either a *maf'ul li-ajlihi* (object of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and reminder") or as two verbal nouns in the position of a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier), meaning "guiding" and "reminding." "People of understanding" means people of sound intellect.

Then Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient in the face of harm, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah which He made to His messengers is true, with no breach in it and no doubt about its occurrence, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and His saying: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173]. Al-Kalbi said: this was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*ayat al-sayf*, a term for the verse commonly held to abrogate earlier verses calling for forbearance toward the disbelievers).

Then He commanded him, glorified is He, to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was said: the sin here means the sin of your community, so it involves an elided noun (*hadhf mudaf*). It was said: it means minor sins, according to those who permit them for the prophets. It was said: it is merely an act of worship directed to him (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness, for the increase of reward. Allah had already forgiven him what was before and what came after of his sins. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾. That is: remain in glorifying Allah, accompanied by praise of Him. It was also said: it means pray at these two times, the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was also said: they are two prayers, two rak'ahs in the morning and two rak'ahs in the evening, and that was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾. That is: without any clear, manifest proof having come to them from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾. That is: there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance toward the truth, which drives them to deny you. The clause ﴿they will never attain it﴾ (*ma hum bi-balighihi*) is a qualifying clause (*sifah*) for "pride." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain in their desire for it, so he took it to involve an elided noun. Others said: "they will never attain the pride." Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride (*takabbur*) over Muhammad (ﷺ) and greed that they might overcome him, and they will never attain that. It was also said: "pride" here means a great matter, i.e. they seek prophethood, or they seek some great matter by which they might reach you, such as killing, and they will not reach that. Mujahid said: its meaning is, in their breasts is greatness, which they will never attain. The verse refers to the polytheists, and it was also said: the Jews, as its explanation will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

Then Allah commanded him to seek refuge in Allah from their evils, saying: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. That is: turn to Him for refuge from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you. Indeed, He hears their words and sees their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Then He, glorified is He, explained His immense power, saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. That is: it is greater in souls and more magnificent in hearts, because of the enormity of their bodies, their stability without pillars, and the orbits of the spheres moving with the stars without any apparent cause. Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal, when the Jews magnified him. Yahya ibn Salam said: this is an argument against the deniers of resurrection, meaning: they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. Then, after He, glorified is He, mentioned disputing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, saying: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾. That is: the one who disputes with falsehood and the one who disputes with truth. ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the one who does evil﴾. That is: the doer of good through faith and righteous deeds and the doer of evil through disbelief and sins are not equal. ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾. That is: there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence. ﴿But most of mankind do not believe﴾ in it, nor do they affirm it, due to the shortcomings of their understanding and the weakness of their intellects in grasping the proof. The "most of mankind" here means the disbelievers who deny resurrection.

Then, after He, glorified is He, made clear that the establishment of the Hour is true, with no doubt or dubiety about it, He guided His servants to what is the means to happiness in the abode of eternity. It was also said: the call here means asking, i.e. seeking benefit and averting harm.

I say: rather, the second is preferable, because the meaning of *du'a'* literally and in the Law is requesting. If it is used in other than that sense, it is metaphorical. Then He, glorified is He, explicitly stated that this calling, considering its literal meaning, which is requesting, is part of His worship, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾. That is: abased and debased. This is a severe warning for those who are too arrogant to call upon Allah. He is the absolutely Generous, who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and is angry with the one who does not seek from His great bounty and vast dominion what he needs of the affairs of this world and the next. It was said: this promise of response is conditional upon His will, i.e. "I will respond to you if I wish," like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 41]. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, that he said: "The greatness of Quraysh."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, (p-1306) Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilyah*, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* transmitted from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," then he recited: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me..."﴾, and said: "Those too proud to worship Me, i.e., to call upon Me, will enter Hell in humiliation."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib transmitted from al-Bara' that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, supplication is worship. ﴿And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-'Azamah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, that he said: "Affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you."

al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, regarding the verse, that he said: "Worship Me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is seeking forgiveness."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Hakim, and Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, He will be angry with him."

Ahmad, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, and al-Tabarani narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Caution does not benefit against decree, but supplication benefits against what has descended and what has not yet descended, so you must engage in supplication."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, in Nawadir al-Usul, narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The best worship is supplication," and he recited ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari, in al-Adab, narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which worship is best? He said: A person's supplication for himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him follow its saying immediately with "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is His words: ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾. This is part of what Allah, glorified is He, related shortly after His support for His messengers. That is, We gave him the Torah and prophethood, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. Muqatil said: "The guidance from misguidance" means the Torah.

﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book, a guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾. The Book here means the Torah. The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is that when Allah, glorified is He, revealed the Torah to Moses, it remained among them after him, and they inherited it from one generation to the next.

It was also said: the Book here means all the books revealed to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. "A guidance and a reminder" are in the accusative position, as either a *maf'ul li-ajlihi* (object of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and reminder") or as two verbal nouns in the position of a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier), meaning "guiding" and "reminding." "People of understanding" means people of sound intellect.

Then Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient in the face of harm, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah which He made to His messengers is true, with no breach in it and no doubt about its occurrence, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and His saying: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173]. Al-Kalbi said: this was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*ayat al-sayf*, a term for the verse commonly held to abrogate earlier verses calling for forbearance toward the disbelievers).

Then He commanded him, glorified is He, to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was said: the sin here means the sin of your community, so it involves an elided noun (*hadhf mudaf*). It was said: it means minor sins, according to those who permit them for the prophets. It was said: it is merely an act of worship directed to him (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness, for the increase of reward. Allah had already forgiven him what was before and what came after of his sins. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾. That is: remain in glorifying Allah, accompanied by praise of Him. It was also said: it means pray at these two times, the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was also said: they are two prayers, two rak'ahs in the morning and two rak'ahs in the evening, and that was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾. That is: without any clear, manifest proof having come to them from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾. That is: there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance toward the truth, which drives them to deny you. The clause ﴿they will never attain it﴾ (*ma hum bi-balighihi*) is a qualifying clause (*sifah*) for "pride." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain in their desire for it, so he took it to involve an elided noun. Others said: "they will never attain the pride." Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride (*takabbur*) over Muhammad (ﷺ) and greed that they might overcome him, and they will never attain that. It was also said: "pride" here means a great matter, i.e. they seek prophethood, or they seek some great matter by which they might reach you, such as killing, and they will not reach that. Mujahid said: its meaning is, in their breasts is greatness, which they will never attain. The verse refers to the polytheists, and it was also said: the Jews, as its explanation will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

Then Allah commanded him to seek refuge in Allah from their evils, saying: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. That is: turn to Him for refuge from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you. Indeed, He hears their words and sees their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Then He, glorified is He, explained His immense power, saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. That is: it is greater in souls and more magnificent in hearts, because of the enormity of their bodies, their stability without pillars, and the orbits of the spheres moving with the stars without any apparent cause. So how can they deny resurrection and the bringing back to life of what is lesser than them in every respect, as in His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal, when the Jews magnified him. Yahya ibn Salam said: this is an argument against the deniers of resurrection, meaning: they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. (p-1305) ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ the greatness of Allah's power, and that nothing can overcome Him.

Then, after He, glorified is He, mentioned disputing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, saying: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾. That is: the one who disputes with falsehood and the one who disputes with truth. ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the one who does evil﴾. That is: the doer of good through faith and righteous deeds and the doer of evil through disbelief and sins are not equal. The addition of *la* (no) in ﴿nor the evildoer﴾ is for emphasis. ﴿Little do you remember.﴾ The majority read *yatadhakkarun* with a *ya* (third person, the absent), and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading, because what comes before and after it is in the third person, not the second person. The Kufans read it with a *ta* (second person), by way of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person, i.e. "you" instead of "they"), meaning: *taddhakkur* (remembrance), "little do you remember."

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾. That is: there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence. ﴿But most of mankind do not believe﴾ in it, nor do they affirm it, due to the shortcomings of their understanding and the weakness of their intellects in grasping the proof. The "most of mankind" here means the disbelievers who deny resurrection.

Then, after He, glorified is He, made clear that the establishment of the Hour is true, with no doubt or dubiety about it, He guided His servants to what is the means to happiness in the abode of eternity. So He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to relate what He commanded him to convey, which is: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you."﴾ Most of the exegetes said the meaning is: "Make Me one and worship Me, and I will accept your worship and forgive you." It was also said: the call here means asking, i.e. seeking benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the first is preferable, because *du'a'* (calling/supplication) in most usages of the Noble Book means worship. I say: rather, the second is preferable, because the meaning of *du'a'* literally and in the Law is requesting. If it is used in other than that sense, it is metaphorical. Moreover, *du'a'* in itself, considering its literal meaning, is worship; indeed, it is the essence of worship, as the authentic hadith has reported. So Allah, glorified is He, commanded His servants to call upon Him and promised them a response, and His promise is true, and "the word is not changed with Him, nor does He break the promise."

Then He, glorified is He, explicitly stated that this calling, considering its literal meaning, which is requesting, is part of His worship, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾. That is: abased and debased. This is a severe warning for those who are too arrogant to call upon Allah. It contains great gentleness toward His servants and magnificent kindness to them, in that He threatens those who abandon seeking good from Him and seeking protection from evil through Him with this severe threat, and punishes him with this great punishment.

So, O servants of Allah, direct your desires and rely in all your requests upon the One who commanded you to direct them to Him, guided you to rely upon Him, and guaranteed you a response when you call on Him by granting your request. He is the absolutely Generous, who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and is angry with the one who does not seek from His great bounty and vast dominion what he needs of the affairs of this world and the next. It was said: this promise of response is conditional upon His will, i.e. "I will respond to you if I wish," like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 41]. Allah knows best.

The majority read *sayadkhulun* with a *fath* on the *ya* and a *damm* on the *kha*, in the active voice (*mabni lil-fa'il*). Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Warsh, and Abu Ja'far read it with a *damm* on the *ya* and a *fath* on the *kha*, in the passive voice (*mabni lil-maf'ul*).

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned some of what He had bestowed upon His servants, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein﴾ from the movements of seeking livelihood, since He made it dark and cool, suited to rest, by repose and sleep; and ﴿the day giving sight﴾, that is, bright, so that you may see your needs therein and move about in seeking your livelihood. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, bestowing upon them His blessings, which cannot be counted. ﴿But most of mankind are not grateful﴾ for the blessings and do not acknowledge them, either because of their denial of them and disbelief in them, as is the state of the disbelievers, or because of their neglect of reflection and their failure to give the thanks that the Benefactor deserves. These are the ignorant.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him﴾. Glorified is He, in this He demonstrated the perfection of His power, which necessitates the obligation of affirming His Oneness. The majority read *khaliq* (Creator) in the nominative (*raf'*), as a predicate following the first predicate of the subject. Zayd ibn 'Ali read it in the accusative (*nasb*), as a term of specification (*ikhtisas*). ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ That is: how do you turn away from worshipping Him and divert from affirming His Oneness?

﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. That is: like this delusion, those who deny the signs of Allah and reject His Oneness are deluded.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned to them another kind of His blessings which He bestowed upon them, along with what that contains of indication of the perfection of His power and His sole right to divinity, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth as a place of settlement and the sky as a ceiling﴾. That is: a place of settlement in which you live and in which you die, and the sky as a building, meaning a firm, standing roof.

Then He explained some of His blessings concerning the souls of the servants, saying: ﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms﴾. That is: He created you in the best form. Al-Zajjaj said: He created you the best of all living creatures. The majority read *sawwarakum* with a *damm* on the *sad*, and al-A'mash and Abu Razin read it with a *kasra*. Al-Jawhari said: *Siwar* with a *kasra* on the *sad* is a dialect variant of *Suwar* with a *damm*. ﴿And He provided you with good things﴾, that is, the delicious things. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is: the abundance of His goodness and blessing.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Hakim, and Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, He will be angry with him."
