al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, in Nawadir al-Usul, narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The best worship is supplication," and he recited ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari, in al-Adab, narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which worship is best? He said: A person's supplication for himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him follow its saying immediately with "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is His words: ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 40, verses 53–70 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾. This is part of what Allah, glorified is He, related shortly after His support for His messengers. That is, We gave him the Torah and prophethood, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. Muqatil said: "The guidance from misguidance" means the Torah.

﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book, a guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾. The Book here means the Torah. The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is that when Allah, glorified is He, revealed the Torah to Moses, it remained among them after him, and they inherited it from one generation to the next.

It was also said: the Book here means all the books revealed to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. "A guidance and a reminder" are in the accusative position, as either a *maf'ul li-ajlihi* (object of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and reminder") or as two verbal nouns in the position of a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier), meaning "guiding" and "reminding." "People of understanding" means people of sound intellect.

Then Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient in the face of harm, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾. That is: be patient over the harm of the polytheists, just as the messengers before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah which He made to His messengers is true, with no breach in it and no doubt about its occurrence, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and His saying: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173]. Al-Kalbi said: this was abrogated by the verse of the sword (*ayat al-sayf*, a term for the verse commonly held to abrogate earlier verses calling for forbearance toward the disbelievers).

Then He commanded him, glorified is He, to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was said: the sin here means the sin of your community, so it involves an elided noun (*hadhf mudaf*). It was said: it means minor sins, according to those who permit them for the prophets. It was said: it is merely an act of worship directed to him (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness, for the increase of reward. Allah had already forgiven him what was before and what came after of his sins. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾. That is: remain in glorifying Allah, accompanied by praise of Him. It was also said: it means pray at these two times, the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was also said: they are two prayers, two rak'ahs in the morning and two rak'ahs in the evening, and that was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾. That is: without any clear, manifest proof having come to them from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾. That is: there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance toward the truth, which drives them to deny you. The clause ﴿they will never attain it﴾ (*ma hum bi-balighihi*) is a qualifying clause (*sifah*) for "pride." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain in their desire for it, so he took it to involve an elided noun. Others said: "they will never attain the pride." Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except pride (*takabbur*) over Muhammad (ﷺ) and greed that they might overcome him, and they will never attain that. It was also said: "pride" here means a great matter, i.e. they seek prophethood, or they seek some great matter by which they might reach you, such as killing, and they will not reach that. Mujahid said: its meaning is, in their breasts is greatness, which they will never attain. The verse refers to the polytheists, and it was also said: the Jews, as its explanation will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

Then Allah commanded him to seek refuge in Allah from their evils, saying: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. That is: turn to Him for refuge from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you. Indeed, He hears their words and sees their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Then He, glorified is He, explained His immense power, saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾. That is: it is greater in souls and more magnificent in hearts, because of the enormity of their bodies, their stability without pillars, and the orbits of the spheres moving with the stars without any apparent cause. So how can they deny resurrection and the bringing back to life of what is lesser than them in every respect, as in His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. Abu al-'Aliyah said: the meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal, when the Jews magnified him. Yahya ibn Salam said: this is an argument against the deniers of resurrection, meaning: they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. (p-1305) ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ the greatness of Allah's power, and that nothing can overcome Him.

Then, after He, glorified is He, mentioned disputing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, saying: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾. That is: the one who disputes with falsehood and the one who disputes with truth. ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the one who does evil﴾. That is: the doer of good through faith and righteous deeds and the doer of evil through disbelief and sins are not equal. The addition of *la* (no) in ﴿nor the evildoer﴾ is for emphasis. ﴿Little do you remember.﴾ The majority read *yatadhakkarun* with a *ya* (third person, the absent), and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading, because what comes before and after it is in the third person, not the second person. The Kufans read it with a *ta* (second person), by way of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person, i.e. "you" instead of "they"), meaning: *taddhakkur* (remembrance), "little do you remember."

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it﴾. That is: there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence. ﴿But most of mankind do not believe﴾ in it, nor do they affirm it, due to the shortcomings of their understanding and the weakness of their intellects in grasping the proof. The "most of mankind" here means the disbelievers who deny resurrection.

Then, after He, glorified is He, made clear that the establishment of the Hour is true, with no doubt or dubiety about it, He guided His servants to what is the means to happiness in the abode of eternity. So He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to relate what He commanded him to convey, which is: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you."﴾ Most of the exegetes said the meaning is: "Make Me one and worship Me, and I will accept your worship and forgive you." It was also said: the call here means asking, i.e. seeking benefit and averting harm.

It was said: the first is preferable, because *du'a'* (calling/supplication) in most usages of the Noble Book means worship. I say: rather, the second is preferable, because the meaning of *du'a'* literally and in the Law is requesting. If it is used in other than that sense, it is metaphorical. Moreover, *du'a'* in itself, considering its literal meaning, is worship; indeed, it is the essence of worship, as the authentic hadith has reported. So Allah, glorified is He, commanded His servants to call upon Him and promised them a response, and His promise is true, and "the word is not changed with Him, nor does He break the promise."

Then He, glorified is He, explicitly stated that this calling, considering its literal meaning, which is requesting, is part of His worship, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation﴾. That is: abased and debased. This is a severe warning for those who are too arrogant to call upon Allah. It contains great gentleness toward His servants and magnificent kindness to them, in that He threatens those who abandon seeking good from Him and seeking protection from evil through Him with this severe threat, and punishes him with this great punishment.

So, O servants of Allah, direct your desires and rely in all your requests upon the One who commanded you to direct them to Him, guided you to rely upon Him, and guaranteed you a response when you call on Him by granting your request. He is the absolutely Generous, who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and is angry with the one who does not seek from His great bounty and vast dominion what he needs of the affairs of this world and the next. It was said: this promise of response is conditional upon His will, i.e. "I will respond to you if I wish," like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then He will remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 41]. Allah knows best.

The majority read *sayadkhulun* with a *fath* on the *ya* and a *damm* on the *kha*, in the active voice (*mabni lil-fa'il*). Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Warsh, and Abu Ja'far read it with a *damm* on the *ya* and a *fath* on the *kha*, in the passive voice (*mabni lil-maf'ul*).

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned some of what He had bestowed upon His servants, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein﴾ from the movements of seeking livelihood, since He made it dark and cool, suited to rest, by repose and sleep; and ﴿the day giving sight﴾, that is, bright, so that you may see your needs therein and move about in seeking your livelihood. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, bestowing upon them His blessings, which cannot be counted. ﴿But most of mankind are not grateful﴾ for the blessings and do not acknowledge them, either because of their denial of them and disbelief in them, as is the state of the disbelievers, or because of their neglect of reflection and their failure to give the thanks that the Benefactor deserves. These are the ignorant.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him﴾. Glorified is He, in this He demonstrated the perfection of His power, which necessitates the obligation of affirming His Oneness. The majority read *khaliq* (Creator) in the nominative (*raf'*), as a predicate following the first predicate of the subject. Zayd ibn 'Ali read it in the accusative (*nasb*), as a term of specification (*ikhtisas*). ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ That is: how do you turn away from worshipping Him and divert from affirming His Oneness?

﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. That is: like this delusion, those who deny the signs of Allah and reject His Oneness are deluded.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned to them another kind of His blessings which He bestowed upon them, along with what that contains of indication of the perfection of His power and His sole right to divinity, saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth as a place of settlement and the sky as a ceiling﴾. That is: a place of settlement in which you live and in which you die, and the sky as a building, meaning a firm, standing roof.

Then He explained some of His blessings concerning the souls of the servants, saying: ﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms﴾. That is: He created you in the best form. Al-Zajjaj said: He created you the best of all living creatures. The majority read *sawwarakum* with a *damm* on the *sad*, and al-A'mash and Abu Razin read it with a *kasra*. Al-Jawhari said: *Siwar* with a *kasra* on the *sad* is a dialect variant of *Suwar* with a *damm*. ﴿And He provided you with good things﴾, that is, the delicious things. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is: the abundance of His goodness and blessing.

65. ﴿He is the Living; there is no deity except Him﴾. That is: the Everlasting who does not perish, the One singled out for divinity. ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾. That is: in obedience and worship. ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is a statement (*khabar*) and within it is an implied command, meaning: "Praise Him."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it. Al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'The Dajjal will come from among us at the end of time, and he will have authority. So magnify his affair. We will do such-and-such and such-and-such.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain.﴾ He said: 'Whoever says ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ will not attain it.' So He commanded His Prophet to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal. ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ka'b al-Ahbar concerning the verse that he said: "They are the Jews. It was revealed concerning them, regarding what they were awaiting of the affair of the Dajjal."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts except pride﴾, that he said: "The greatness of Quraysh."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, (p-1306) Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilyah*, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* transmitted from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," then he recited: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me..."﴾, and said: "Those too proud to worship Me, i.e., to call upon Me, will enter Hell in humiliation."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib transmitted from al-Bara' that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, supplication is worship. ﴿And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-'Azamah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, that he said: "Affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you."

al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, regarding the verse, that he said: "Worship Me."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is seeking forgiveness."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Hakim, and Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, He will be angry with him."

Ahmad, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, and al-Tabarani narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Caution does not benefit against decree, but supplication benefits against what has descended and what has not yet descended, so you must engage in supplication."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, in Nawadir al-Usul, narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The best worship is supplication," and he recited ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari, in al-Adab, narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which worship is best? He said: A person's supplication for himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him follow its saying immediately with "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is His words: ﴿So call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Almighty God commanded His Messenger to inform the polytheists that God had forbidden him to worship other than Him, and had commanded him to uphold tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness). So He said: ﴿Say: I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides God﴾, meaning the idols.

Then He explained the reason for the prohibition, saying: ﴿When the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord﴾, meaning the rational and transmitted evidences, for they necessitate tawhid. ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., to surrender to Him in obedience and humility.

Then He followed this with mention of one of the proofs of tawhid, saying: ﴿It is He who created you from dust﴾, i.e., created your first father, Adam, and his creation from dust necessitates the creation of his offspring from it. ﴿Then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot﴾. The explanation of this has already been given in more than one place. ﴿Then He brings you out as a child﴾, i.e., as children; it is stated in the singular because it is a collective noun, or in the sense that He brings out each one of you as a child. ﴿Then that you may reach your maturity﴾, which is the state in which strength and intellect are combined. The explanation of "ashudd" (maturity) has been given fully in Surat al-An'am. The lam of purpose (al-lam al-ta'liliyyah) in ﴿that you may reach﴾ is coordinated with another purpose, [parallel to] "to bring you out," and the implied meaning is: that you may grow up little by little, then that you may reach the utmost perfection. His saying: ﴿Then that you may become elders﴾ is coordinated with "that you may reach." Nafi', Hafs, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Muhaysin and Hisham read ﴿shuyukhan﴾ with a dammah on the shin, while the rest read it with a kasrah. It has also been read "shaykhan" in the singular, corresponding to "tifl" (child). The shaykh (elder) is one who has passed forty years of age. ﴿And among you is one who dies before that﴾, i.e., before old age. ﴿And that you may reach an appointed term﴾, i.e., the time of death or the Day of Resurrection; the lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). ﴿And perhaps you will reason﴾, i.e., so that you may understand the oneness of your Lord and His overwhelming power in creating you through these varied stages.

﴿It is He who gives life and causes death﴾, i.e., He is able to give life and cause death. ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ of the matters He wills, ﴿then He only says to it: "Be," and it is﴾ without any delay. This is an illustration of the effect of His power on things that can be done when His will is directed toward them. Its real meaning has already been verified in al-Baqarah and what follows it.

Then He marvelled, glorified be He, at the state of those who dispute concerning the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ The meaning of disputation has already been explained. ﴿How are they turned away?﴾, i.e., (p-1307) how are they diverted from them, despite the presence of the proofs indicating their validity, and that in themselves they necessitate tawhid?

Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Who have denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the exegetes said it was revealed concerning the Qadariyyah. Ibn Sirin said: If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyyah, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed.

This is answered by saying that God, glorified be He, has described these people with an attribute that indicates something other than what they said, when He said: ﴿Who have denied the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. This is a description that cannot correctly be applied to a sect within the sects of Islam. The relative pronoun is either in the genitive position as an attribute of the first relative pronoun, or a substitute for it. It may also be in the accusative position as a condemnation. The "Book" means either the Qur'an or the genus of revealed books from God. His saying: ﴿and what We sent with Our messengers﴾ is coordinated with "the Book," and it refers to what was revealed to the messengers without a book, if the lam in "al-Kitab" is for genus, or to the rest of the books, if "al-Kitab" means the Qur'an. ﴿But they will come to know﴾ the outcome of their affair and the evil consequence of their disbelief. In this is a severe warning.

The adverbial phrase in His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks﴾ is connected to ﴿they will come to know﴾, i.e., they will come to know at the time when the shackles are around their necks. The "chains" are coordinated with "the shackles," and the full sense is: when the shackles and chains are around their necks. It is permissible for "chains" to be in the nominative as a subject whose predicate is omitted, the indication being "around their necks." It is also permissible that its predicate is ﴿they are dragged in the boiling water﴾ with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., they are dragged with them in the boiling water. This is according to the reading of the majority, with "chains" in the nominative. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah and Abu al-Jawza' read it in the accusative, and they read "yusjabun" with a fathah on the ya' in the active voice, so "chains" becomes a fronted object. Some read "chains" in the genitive.

Al-Farra' said: This reading is interpreted according to meaning, since the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning according to this reading is: "and in the chains they are dragged." Ibn al-Anbari objected to this, saying that this is not permissible in Arabic. The position of "yusjabun" is, on the assumption that "chains" is coordinated with "shackles," in the accusative; and on the assumption that "chains" is a subject whose predicate is "around their necks," in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; or it has no position, but is a resumptive sentence answering an implied question.

The "hamim" is that which is at extreme heat; it is said also to be pus, and its explanation has already been given. ﴿Then in the Fire they are kindled﴾. It is said: I set the oven alight (sajartu al-tannur), i.e., I kindled it, and sajjartuhu, I filled it with fuel; from this is ﴿and the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, i.e., filled. The meaning is: the Fire is kindled with them, or it is filled with them. Mujahid and Muqatil said: The Fire is kindled with them, and they become its fuel.

﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those whom you used to worship besides God?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them, i.e., where are the partners whom you used to worship besides God?

﴿They will say: They have vanished from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and we have lost them, so we do not see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to report their non-existence, that they have no reality. So they said: ﴿Rather, we used not to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., we used not to worship anything. They said this when it became clear to them the error and ignorance they had been in, and that they used to worship what neither sees nor hears, neither harms nor benefits. This is not a denial from them of the existence of the idols they used to worship, but a confession that their worship of them was false. ﴿Thus God leads astray the disbelievers﴾, i.e., like that misguidance God leads astray the disbelievers, in that they worshipped these idols which brought them to the Fire.

The reference in His saying "That is because..." is to the misguidance implied by the verb, i.e., that misguidance is due to ﴿what you used to exult in on earth﴾, i.e., what you used to show in the world of joy at disobeying God and delight in opposing His messengers and books. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of wealth, followers and health. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of denying the Resurrection. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

Mujahid and others said: "tamrahun" means you act insolently and wantonly. Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is gladness and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. Muqatil said: "al-maraḥ" is insolence and conceit.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein﴾, i.e., as those who intend to remain in it forever. ﴿Evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾ who refuse to accept the truth: Hell.

Then Almighty God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of God is true﴾, i.e., His promise to take vengeance upon them is certain to occur, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Hence He said: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾ of punishment in this world by killing, capture and subjugation, and what is in "fa-imma" is superfluous according to the view of al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj; the original was "fa-in nurika." The energetic nun was attached to the verb. His saying: ﴿or We cause you to die﴾ is coordinated with "We show you," i.e., or We cause you to die before the punishment descends upon them. ﴿Then to Us they will be returned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and We will punish them.

﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you﴾, i.e., We have informed you of their news and what they encountered from their peoples. ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God﴾, not on his own initiative. The "sign" means the miracle that indicates his prophethood. ﴿So when the command of God comes, it will be concluded with truth﴾, i.e., when the appointed time of their punishment comes, in this world or the Hereafter, judgment will be given among them in truth, so God, by His just decree, saves His righteous servants. ﴿And the falsifiers will lose there﴾, i.e., at that time, those who follow falsehood and act upon it.

Then God, glorified be He, showed favour to His servants with one kind of His countless blessings, saying: ﴿God is He who made for you the cattle that you may ride some of them and eat from them﴾, i.e., He created them for your sake. Al-Zajjaj said: "al-an'am" here means camels. It is also said: the eight pairs. ﴿That you may ride some of them﴾; "min" here is partitive, and likewise in His saying ﴿and from them you eat﴾. It is also permissible that "min" be for the beginning of the limit in both places, the meaning being: the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating; but the first is preferable. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

﴿And for you in them are other benefits﴾, He postponed mention of benefits other than riding and eating: wool, fleece, hair, butter, ghee, cheese and other things. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another, and this has already been fully explained in Surat al-Nahl. ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (p-1308) i.e., upon camels on land, and upon ships at sea.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, i.e., His indications that point to the perfection of His power and His oneness. ﴿So which of God's signs will you deny?﴾ For they are all so manifest and so undisguised that no denier can deny them and no rejecter can reject them. In this is a rebuke and a great reproach to them. The "ayya" is governed by "tunkiruna" (you deny), and it was placed before the governing verb because it has the front position of the sentence.

Then He guided them, glorified be He, to reflection and contemplation upon the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied their messengers. Then He explained, glorified be He, that those nations were superior to these in number and strength, saying: ﴿They were more numerous than them and greater in strength﴾, i.e., more numerous in quantity, stronger in bodies, wealthier in possessions, and more prominent in traces on earth through their buildings, fortresses and cultivation. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾. "Ma" in the first place may be interrogative, meaning: what thing availed them? Or negative, meaning: it did not avail them. The second "ma" may be relative or verbal (masdariyyah).

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with clear arguments and manifest miracles, ﴿they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, i.e., they displayed joy in what they had of what they claimed to be knowledge, of deceptive doubts and deviant claims. Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 40, verse 71–85 (part 2 of 2):

﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾. That is, the way that has already gone by among His servants. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein﴾, i.e., as those who intend to remain in it forever. ﴿Evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾ who refuse to accept the truth: Hell.

﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those whom you used to worship besides God?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them, i.e., where are the partners whom you used to worship besides God?

﴿They will say: They have vanished from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and we have lost them, so we do not see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to report their non-existence, that they have no reality. So they said: ﴿Rather, we used not to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., we used not to worship anything. They said this when it became clear to them the error and ignorance they had been in, and that they used to worship what neither sees nor hears, neither harms nor benefits. This is not a denial from them of the existence of the idols they used to worship, but a confession that their worship of them was false. ﴿Thus God leads astray the disbelievers﴾, i.e., like that misguidance God leads astray the disbelievers, in that they worshipped these idols which brought them to the Fire.

The reference in His saying "That is because..." is to the misguidance implied by the verb, i.e., that misguidance is due to ﴿what you used to exult in on earth﴾, i.e., what you used to show in the world of joy at disobeying God and delight in opposing His messengers and books. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of wealth, followers and health. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of denying the Resurrection. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

Mujahid and others said: "tamrahun" means you act insolently and wantonly. Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is gladness and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. Muqatil said: "al-maraḥ" is insolence and conceit.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein﴾, i.e., as those who intend to remain in it forever. ﴿Evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾ who refuse to accept the truth: Hell.

Then Almighty God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of God is true﴾, i.e., His promise to take vengeance upon them is certain to occur, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Hence He said: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾ of punishment in this world by killing, capture and subjugation, and what is in "fa-imma" is superfluous according to the view of al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj; the original was "fa-in nurika." The energetic nun was attached to the verb. His saying: ﴿or We cause you to die﴾ is coordinated with "We show you," i.e., or We cause you to die before the punishment descends upon them. ﴿Then to Us they will be returned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and We will punish them.

﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you﴾, i.e., We have informed you of their news and what they encountered from their peoples. ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God﴾, not on his own initiative. The "sign" means the miracle that indicates his prophethood. ﴿So when the command of God comes, it will be concluded with truth﴾, i.e., when the appointed time of their punishment comes, in this world or the Hereafter, judgment will be given among them in truth, so God, by His just decree, saves His righteous servants. ﴿And the falsifiers will lose there﴾, i.e., at that time, those who follow falsehood and act upon it.

Then God, glorified be He, showed favour to His servants with one kind of His countless blessings, saying: ﴿God is He who made for you the cattle that you may ride some of them and eat from them﴾, i.e., He created them for your sake. Al-Zajjaj said: "al-an'am" here means camels. It is also said: the eight pairs. ﴿That you may ride some of them﴾; "min" here is partitive, and likewise in His saying ﴿and from them you eat﴾. It is also permissible that "min" be for the beginning of the limit in both places, the meaning being: the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating; but the first is preferable. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

﴿And for you in them are other benefits﴾, He postponed mention of benefits other than riding and eating: wool, fleece, hair, butter, ghee, cheese and other things. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another, and this has already been fully explained in Surat al-Nahl. ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (p-1308) i.e., upon camels on land, and upon ships at sea.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, i.e., His indications that point to the perfection of His power and His oneness. ﴿So which of God's signs will you deny?﴾ For they are all so manifest and so undisguised that no denier can deny them and no rejecter can reject them. In this is a rebuke and a great reproach to them. The "ayya" is governed by "tunkiruna" (you deny), and it was placed before the governing verb because it has the front position of the sentence.

Then He guided them, glorified be He, to reflection and contemplation upon the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied their messengers. The traces that exist in their dwellings indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end to which they came.

Then He explained, glorified be He, that those nations were superior to these in number and strength, saying: ﴿They were more numerous than them and greater in strength﴾, i.e., more numerous in quantity, stronger in bodies, wealthier in possessions, and more prominent in traces on earth through their buildings, fortresses and cultivation. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾. "Ma" in the first place may be interrogative, meaning: what thing availed them? Or negative, meaning: it did not avail them. The second "ma" may be relative or verbal (masdariyyah).

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with clear arguments and manifest miracles, ﴿they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, i.e., they displayed joy in what they had of what they claimed to be knowledge, of deceptive doubts and deviant claims. He called it knowledge in mockery of them, or according to what they believed.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." It is also said: the intended meaning is knowledge of worldly affairs, not religion, as in His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾ [al-Rum: 7]. It is also said: those who rejoiced in what knowledge they had were the messengers themselves, for when their people denied them, God informed them that He would destroy the disbelievers and save the believers, so they rejoiced at that. ﴿And there encompassed them what they used to mock﴾, i.e., the recompense of their mockery surrounded them.

That is, the way that has already gone by among His servants. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, established this way among all nations: that faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment.

The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa' and Surat al-Tawba. The accusative of ﴿sunnata﴾ is because it is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing a deleted verb, like "the promise of Allah" and similar emphatic verbal nouns.

It was said: it is accusative as a warning, meaning: beware, O people of Makkah, of the way of Allah with the earlier nations. The first is better. ﴿And the disbelievers will lose there﴾. That is, at the time of their seeing the might of Allah and witnessing His punishment.

Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss becomes clear to them when they see the punishment.

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Hakim (who graded it sahih), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿When the shackles are around their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿they will be burned in the fire﴾, then said: If a lump like this one (and he gestured to a skull) were sent down from the sky to the earth, which is a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before night. And if it were sent from the top of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its bottom, or he said its depth."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Nar narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "They will swim in the boiling water, and every part of them will be stripped away, skin, flesh and sinew, until it reaches the heel, until its flesh is measured, and its length is sixty cubits. Then they will be clothed in another skin, and then they will be dragged into the boiling water."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib regarding His words ﴿And among them are those We have not related to you﴾, he said: "Allah sent an Abyssinian slave, and he is among those whom He did not relate to Muhammad."

It has also been read "shaykhan" in the singular, corresponding to "tifl" (child). The shaykh (elder) is one who has passed forty years of age. ﴿And among you is one who dies before that﴾, i.e., before old age. ﴿And that you may reach an appointed term﴾, i.e., the time of death or the Day of Resurrection; the lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). ﴿And perhaps you will reason﴾, i.e., so that you may understand the oneness of your Lord and His overwhelming power in creating you through these varied stages.

﴿It is He who gives life and causes death﴾, i.e., He is able to give life and cause death. ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ of the matters He wills, ﴿then He only says to it: "Be," and it is﴾ without any delay. This is an illustration of the effect of His power on things that can be done when His will is directed toward them. Its real meaning has already been verified in al-Baqarah and what follows it.

Then He marvelled, glorified be He, at the state of those who dispute concerning the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Who have denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the exegetes said it was revealed concerning the Qadariyyah. Ibn Sirin said: If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyyah, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed.

This is answered by saying that God, glorified be He, has described these people with an attribute that indicates something other than what they said, when He said: ﴿Who have denied the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. This is a description that cannot correctly be applied to a sect within the sects of Islam. The relative pronoun is either in the genitive position as an attribute of the first relative pronoun, or a substitute for it. It may also be in the accusative position as a condemnation. The "Book" means either the Qur'an or the genus of revealed books from God. His saying: ﴿and what We sent with Our messengers﴾ is coordinated with "the Book," and it refers to what was revealed to the messengers without a book, if the lam in "al-Kitab" is for genus, or to the rest of the books, if "al-Kitab" means the Qur'an. ﴿But they will come to know﴾ the outcome of their affair and the evil consequence of their disbelief. In this is a severe warning.

The adverbial phrase in His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks﴾ is connected to ﴿they will come to know﴾, i.e., they will come to know at the time when the shackles are around their necks. The "chains" are coordinated with "the shackles," and the full sense is: when the shackles and chains are around their necks. It is permissible for "chains" to be in the nominative as a subject whose predicate is omitted, the indication being "around their necks." It is also permissible that its predicate is ﴿they are dragged in the boiling water﴾ with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., they are dragged with them in the boiling water. This is according to the reading of the majority, with "chains" in the nominative. Some read "chains" in the genitive.

Al-Farra' said: This reading is interpreted according to meaning, since the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning according to this reading is: "and in the chains they are dragged." Ibn al-Anbari objected to this, saying that this is not permissible in Arabic. The position of "yusjabun" is, on the assumption that "chains" is coordinated with "shackles," in the accusative; and on the assumption that "chains" is a subject whose predicate is "around their necks," in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; or it has no position, but is a resumptive sentence answering an implied question.

The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

The traces that exist in their dwellings indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end to which they came.

He called it knowledge in mockery of them, or according to what they believed.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." It is also said: the intended meaning is knowledge of worldly affairs, not religion, as in His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾ [al-Rum: 7]. It is also permissible that "min" be for the beginning of the limit in both places, the meaning being: the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating; but the first is preferable. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

﴿And for you in them are other benefits﴾, He postponed mention of benefits other than riding and eating: wool, fleece, hair, butter, ghee, cheese and other things. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another, and this has already been fully explained in Surat al-Nahl. ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (p-1308) i.e., upon camels on land, and upon ships at sea.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, i.e., His indications that point to the perfection of His power and His oneness. ﴿So which of God's signs will you deny?﴾ For they are all so manifest and so undisguised that no denier can deny them and no rejecter can reject them. In this is a rebuke and a great reproach to them. The "ayya" is governed by "tunkiruna" (you deny), and it was placed before the governing verb because it has the front position of the sentence.

Then He guided them, glorified be He, to reflection and contemplation upon the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied their messengers. The traces that exist in their dwellings indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end to which they came.

Then He explained, glorified be He, that those nations were superior to these in number and strength, saying: ﴿They were more numerous than them and greater in strength﴾, i.e., more numerous in quantity, stronger in bodies, wealthier in possessions, and more prominent in traces on earth through their buildings, fortresses and cultivation. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾. "Ma" in the first place may be interrogative, meaning: what thing availed them? Or negative, meaning: it did not avail them. The second "ma" may be relative or verbal (masdariyyah).

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with clear arguments and manifest miracles, ﴿they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, i.e., they displayed joy in what they had of what they claimed to be knowledge, of deceptive doubts and deviant claims. He called it knowledge in mockery of them, or according to what they believed.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 40, verse 71–85 (part 2 of 2):

﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾. That is, the way that has already gone by among His servants. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, established this way among all nations: that faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment.

The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa' and Surat al-Tawba. The accusative of ﴿sunnata﴾ is because it is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing a deleted verb, like "the promise of Allah" and similar emphatic verbal nouns.

Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss becomes clear to them when they see the punishment.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Nar narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "They will swim in the boiling water, and every part of them will be stripped away, skin, flesh and sinew, until it reaches the heel, until its flesh is measured, and its length is sixty cubits. The meaning is: the Fire is kindled with them, or it is filled with them. Mujahid and Muqatil said: The Fire is kindled with them, and they become its fuel.

﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those whom you used to worship besides God?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them, i.e., where are the partners whom you used to worship besides God?

﴿They will say: They have vanished from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and we have lost them, so we do not see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to report their non-existence, that they have no reality. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein﴾, i.e., as those who intend to remain in it forever. ﴿Evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾ who refuse to accept the truth: Hell.

It is said: I set the oven alight (sajartu al-tannur), i.e., I kindled it, and sajjartuhu, I filled it with fuel; from this is ﴿and the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, i.e., filled. ﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those whom you used to worship besides God?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them, i.e., where are the partners whom you used to worship besides God?

﴿They will say: They have vanished from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and we have lost them, so we do not see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to report their non-existence, that they have no reality. So they said: ﴿Rather, we used not to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., we used not to worship anything. They said this when it became clear to them the error and ignorance they had been in, and that they used to worship what neither sees nor hears, neither harms nor benefits. This is not a denial from them of the existence of the idols they used to worship, but a confession that their worship of them was false. ﴿Thus God leads astray the disbelievers﴾, i.e., like that misguidance God leads astray the disbelievers, in that they worshipped these idols which brought them to the Fire.

It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of wealth, followers and health. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of denying the Resurrection. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

Mujahid and others said: "tamrahun" means you act insolently and wantonly. Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is gladness and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. Muqatil said: "al-maraḥ" is insolence and conceit.

The relative pronoun is either in the genitive position as an attribute of the first relative pronoun, or a substitute for it. It may also be in the accusative position as a condemnation. The "Book" means either the Qur'an or the genus of revealed books from God. The shaykh (elder) is one who has passed forty years of age. ﴿And among you is one who dies before that﴾, i.e., before old age. ﴿And that you may reach an appointed term﴾, i.e., the time of death or the Day of Resurrection; the lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). ﴿And perhaps you will reason﴾, i.e., so that you may understand the oneness of your Lord and His overwhelming power in creating you through these varied stages.

﴿It is He who gives life and causes death﴾, i.e., He is able to give life and cause death. ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ of the matters He wills, ﴿then He only says to it: "Be," and it is﴾ without any delay. This is an illustration of the effect of His power on things that can be done when His will is directed toward them. Its real meaning has already been verified in al-Baqarah and what follows it.

Then He marvelled, glorified be He, at the state of those who dispute concerning the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ The meaning of disputation has already been explained. ﴿How are they turned away?﴾, i.e., (p-1307) how are they diverted from them, despite the presence of the proofs indicating their validity, and that in themselves they necessitate tawhid?

Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Who have denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the exegetes said it was revealed concerning the Qadariyyah. Ibn Sirin said: If this verse was not revealed concerning the Qadariyyah, then I do not know concerning whom it was revealed.

This is answered by saying that God, glorified be He, has described these people with an attribute that indicates something other than what they said, when He said: ﴿Who have denied the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. This is a description that cannot correctly be applied to a sect within the sects of Islam. The relative pronoun is either in the genitive position as an attribute of the first relative pronoun, or a substitute for it. It may also be in the accusative position as a condemnation. The "Book" means either the Qur'an or the genus of revealed books from God. His saying: ﴿and what We sent with Our messengers﴾ is coordinated with "the Book," and it refers to what was revealed to the messengers without a book, if the lam in "al-Kitab" is for genus, or to the rest of the books, if "al-Kitab" means the Qur'an. ﴿But they will come to know﴾ the outcome of their affair and the evil consequence of their disbelief. In this is a severe warning.

The "chains" are coordinated with "the shackles," and the full sense is: when the shackles and chains are around their necks. It is permissible for "chains" to be in the nominative as a subject whose predicate is omitted, the indication being "around their necks." It is also permissible that its predicate is ﴿they are dragged in the boiling water﴾ with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., they are dragged with them in the boiling water. This is according to the reading of the majority, with "chains" in the nominative. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah and Abu al-Jawza' read it in the accusative, and they read "yusjabun" with a fathah on the ya' in the active voice, so "chains" becomes a fronted object. Some read "chains" in the genitive.

Al-Farra' said: This reading is interpreted according to meaning, since the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning according to this reading is: "and in the chains they are dragged." Ibn al-Anbari objected to this, saying that this is not permissible in Arabic. The position of "yusjabun" is, on the assumption that "chains" is coordinated with "shackles," in the accusative; and on the assumption that "chains" is a subject whose predicate is "around their necks," in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; or it has no position, but is a resumptive sentence answering an implied question.

The "hamim" is that which is at extreme heat; it is said also to be pus, and its explanation has already been given. ﴿Then in the Fire they are kindled﴾. It is said: I set the oven alight (sajartu al-tannur), i.e., I kindled it, and sajjartuhu, I filled it with fuel; from this is ﴿and the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, i.e., filled. The meaning is: the Fire is kindled with them, or it is filled with them. Mujahid and Muqatil said: The Fire is kindled with them, and they become its fuel.

﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those whom you used to worship besides God?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach to them, i.e., where are the partners whom you used to worship besides God?

﴿They will say: They have vanished from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and we have lost them, so we do not see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to report their non-existence, that they have no reality. So they said: ﴿Rather, we used not to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., we used not to worship anything. They said this when it became clear to them the error and ignorance they had been in, and that they used to worship what neither sees nor hears, neither harms nor benefits. This is not a denial from them of the existence of the idols they used to worship, but a confession that their worship of them was false. ﴿Thus God leads astray the disbelievers﴾, i.e., like that misguidance God leads astray the disbelievers, in that they worshipped these idols which brought them to the Fire.

The reference in His saying "That is because..." is to the misguidance implied by the verb, i.e., that misguidance is due to ﴿what you used to exult in on earth﴾, i.e., what you used to show in the world of joy at disobeying God and delight in opposing His messengers and books. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of wealth, followers and health. It is also said: what you used to rejoice in of denying the Resurrection. It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

Mujahid and others said: "tamrahun" means you act insolently and wantonly. Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is gladness and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. Muqatil said: "al-maraḥ" is insolence and conceit.

It is also permissible that "min" be for the beginning of the limit in both places, the meaning being: the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating; but the first is preferable. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another, and this has already been fully explained in Surat al-Nahl. ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (p-1308) i.e., upon camels on land, and upon ships at sea.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." It is also said: the intended meaning is knowledge of worldly affairs, not religion, as in His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾ [al-Rum: 7]. That is, the way that has already gone by among His servants. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, established this way among all nations: that faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment.

The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa' and Surat al-Tawba. The accusative of ﴿sunnata﴾ is because it is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing a deleted verb, like "the promise of Allah" and similar emphatic verbal nouns.

It was said: it is accusative as a warning, meaning: beware, O people of Makkah, of the way of Allah with the earlier nations. The first is better. ﴿And the disbelievers will lose there﴾. That is, at the time of their seeing the might of Allah and witnessing His punishment.

Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss becomes clear to them when they see the punishment.

Then He explained the reason for the prohibition, saying: ﴿When the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord﴾, meaning the rational and transmitted evidences, for they necessitate tawhid. ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., to surrender to Him in obedience and humility.

Then He marvelled, glorified be He, at the state of those who dispute concerning the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? It is also said: the "joy" here means insolence and arrogance, and the "exultation" means an increase in insolence.

The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

In this is a rebuke and a great reproach to them. The "ayya" is governed by "tunkiruna" (you deny), and it was placed before the governing verb because it has the front position of the sentence.

Then He guided them, glorified be He, to reflection and contemplation upon the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied their messengers. The traces that exist in their dwellings indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end to which they came.

He called it knowledge in mockery of them, or according to what they believed.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." ﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you﴾, i.e., We have informed you of their news and what they encountered from their peoples. ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God﴾, not on his own initiative. The "sign" means the miracle that indicates his prophethood. ﴿So when the command of God comes, it will be concluded with truth﴾, i.e., when the appointed time of their punishment comes, in this world or the Hereafter, judgment will be given among them in truth, so God, by His just decree, saves His righteous servants. ﴿And the falsifiers will lose there﴾, i.e., at that time, those who follow falsehood and act upon it.

Then God, glorified be He, showed favour to His servants with one kind of His countless blessings, saying: ﴿God is He who made for you the cattle that you may ride some of them and eat from them﴾, i.e., He created them for your sake. Al-Zajjaj said: "al-an'am" here means camels. It is also said: the eight pairs. ﴿That you may ride some of them﴾; "min" here is partitive, and likewise in His saying ﴿and from them you eat﴾. It is also permissible that "min" be for the beginning of the limit in both places, the meaning being: the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating; but the first is preferable. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.

﴿And for you in them are other benefits﴾, He postponed mention of benefits other than riding and eating: wool, fleece, hair, butter, ghee, cheese and other things. ﴿And that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another, and this has already been fully explained in Surat al-Nahl. ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (p-1308) i.e., upon camels on land, and upon ships at sea.

It is also said: the intended meaning of being carried upon the cattle here is the carrying of children and women in litters.

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, i.e., His indications that point to the perfection of His power and His oneness. ﴿So which of God's signs will you deny?﴾ For they are all so manifest and so undisguised that no denier can deny them and no rejecter can reject them. In this is a rebuke and a great reproach to them. The "ayya" is governed by "tunkiruna" (you deny), and it was placed before the governing verb because it has the front position of the sentence.

Then He guided them, glorified be He, to reflection and contemplation upon the signs of God, saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied their messengers. The traces that exist in their dwellings indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end to which they came.

Then He explained, glorified be He, that those nations were superior to these in number and strength, saying: ﴿They were more numerous than them and greater in strength﴾, i.e., more numerous in quantity, stronger in bodies, wealthier in possessions, and more prominent in traces on earth through their buildings, fortresses and cultivation. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾. "Ma" in the first place may be interrogative, meaning: what thing availed them? Or negative, meaning: it did not avail them. The second "ma" may be relative or verbal (masdariyyah).

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with clear arguments and manifest miracles, ﴿they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, i.e., they displayed joy in what they had of what they claimed to be knowledge, of deceptive doubts and deviant claims. He called it knowledge in mockery of them, or according to what they believed.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." It is also said: the intended meaning is knowledge of worldly affairs, not religion, as in His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾ [al-Rum: 7]. It is also said: those who rejoiced in what knowledge they had were the messengers themselves, for when their people denied them, God informed them that He would destroy the disbelievers and save the believers, so they rejoiced at that. ﴿And there encompassed them what they used to mock﴾, i.e., the recompense of their mockery surrounded them.

﴿So when they saw Our might﴾, i.e., they witnessed Our punishment descending upon them, ﴿they said: We believe in God alone and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him﴾, namely the idols they used to worship.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 40, verse 71–85 (part 2 of 2):

﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾. That is, at the time of witnessing Our punishment, because that faith is not the beneficial faith for its possessor, since what benefits is the faith that is chosen (al-iman al-ikhtiyari), not the faith that is compelled (al-iman al-idtirari). ﴿The way of Allah that has passed among His servants﴾. That is, the way that has already gone by among His servants. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, established this way among all nations: that faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment.

The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa' and Surat al-Tawba. The accusative of ﴿sunnata﴾ is because it is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing a deleted verb, like "the promise of Allah" and similar emphatic verbal nouns.

It was said: it is accusative as a warning, meaning: beware, O people of Makkah, of the way of Allah with the earlier nations. The first is better. ﴿And the disbelievers will lose there﴾. That is, at the time of their seeing the might of Allah and witnessing His punishment.

Al-Zajjaj said: the disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss becomes clear to them when they see the punishment.

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Hakim (who graded it sahih), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿When the shackles are around their necks﴾ up to His words ﴿they will be burned in the fire﴾, then said: If a lump like this one (and he gestured to a skull) were sent down from the sky to the earth, which is a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before night. And if it were sent from the top of the chain, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its bottom, or he said its depth."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Nar narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "They will swim in the boiling water, and every part of them will be stripped away, skin, flesh and sinew, until it reaches the heel, until its flesh is measured, and its length is sixty cubits. Then they will be clothed in another skin, and then they will be dragged into the boiling water."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib regarding His words ﴿And among them are those We have not related to you﴾, he said: "Allah sent an Abyssinian slave, and he is among those whom He did not relate to Muhammad."
